top.title: 'Is he crying?': Ajinkya Rahane & Murali Kartik slam India team selection as Mohammed Siraj appears emotional after being dropped for 2nd Test vs NZ
top.description: 'Is he crying?': Ajinkya Rahane & Murali Kartik slam India team selection as Mohammed Siraj appears emotional after being dropped for 2nd Test vs NZ originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mohammed Siraj was missing again in Christchurch against New Zealand. Ajinkya Rahane & Murali Kartik hit out at what the television cameras showed. The selection call has raised fresh questions about India's long-term thinking. 'What's the point then?' Murali Kartik tears into India team management over repeated snubs to an emotional Mohammed Siraj in Christchurch Mohammed Siraj, once again left out of India's playing XI, looked visibly distraught and emotional on the opening morning of the second Test in Christchurch, and Ajinkya Rahane and Murali Kartik didn't hold back on live commentary. Since his Test debut at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG) in 2020, Siraj has featured in every full away series India has played, but the team management decided not to pick him at Hagley Oval, ending that run. The decision has drawn plenty of attention because of the numbers behind it. The 32-year-old leads India's wicket-taking list in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle with 43 scalps from 11 matches, which makes his omission harder for critics to understand. It also comes after a frustrating Test in Wellington, where India kept New Zealand under pressure for long stretches but couldn't bowl the hosts out in the second innings, and the game finished as a draw. Captain Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to bowl first on a surface with a green tinge. India made one change to the seam attack, dropping Prasidh Krishna and handing a maiden Test cap, number 321, to 26-year-old Punjab pacer Gurnoor Brar. Ravindra Jadeja was also left out again, along with Siraj. Murali Kartik on Siraj's heart-on-sleeve mindset after the India snub Rahane was the first to react when the cameras caught Siraj covering his eyes with shades to hide his emotions. "These visuals, is he crying?" Rahane asked. Kartik picked up the thread and drew on his own years in dressing rooms, where reactions to being dropped vary a lot from person to person. "I don't know, brother. He certainly looks quite emotional to me, because he is an emotional person," Kartik began. "Obviously, it hurts. Look, we have always played alongside all kinds of players; some are okay with it; there are some people who are fine when you drop them. "And then there are some people who just want to play; it doesn't matter to them if they have pain in their leg, pain in their head, pain in their body, or shivering, they'll give everything they've got. They put their life on the line. He seems like that kind of bowler." More to follow...

The organization’s relative youth may help explain why. Thirty-three years sounds like a long time until you compare it with the histories of the NFL, NBA, MLB and NHL. Growing pains are to be expected, even with those leagues providing lessons to draw from. Besides, the UFC deals with unusually volatile personalities. These are people who try to hurt each other while wearing what amounts to underwear. That doesn’t excuse the UFC’s faults. There are plenty, and the promotion has made little or no effort to address some of them. But it seems fair to acknowledge what it does well. It’s the premier MMA organization for a reason, and most of us complaining have spent plenty of time watching its product. I hope nobody reading this watches the UFC solely to hate-watch. That sounds like a miserable way to spend a Saturday. Paramount+ makes watching the UFC simpler and potentially cheaper In the spirit of Thanksgiving, let’s consider what the UFC gives the MMA community. For starters, it consistently produces many of the sport’s most entertaining fights. That comes with trade-offs the promotion is frequently criticized for. A couple of decades ago, Fight of the Year candidates could come from almost anywhere. Pride Fighting Championships and HooknShoot delivered memorable bouts around the turn of the century. Strikeforce and Bellator MMA later provided plenty of competition. The Professional Fighters League and Rizin Fighting Federation still produce excellent fights, but the UFC now dominates much of the annual conversation. I think part of that comes from its reluctance to promote -- or sometimes even sign -- fighters whose styles don’t appeal to casual viewers. If entertainment is your priority, that approach has obvious benefits. If you’re primarily interested in discovering who the best fighters are, it’s more frustrating. top.title: Five Levski fans taken to hospital as presidents condemn Marseille violence
top.description: Marseille police said 11 people were injured in the clashes, all of them Bulgarian (Justine MEDDAH) Five Levski Sofia supporters were taken to hospital after violence ahead of the Europa League game at Marseille on Thursday, with the French and Bulgarian presidents blaming the home fans. The lead-up to the match at the Stade Vélodrome was marred by confrontations in the stands between the two sets of fans, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. French President Emmanuel Macron condemned "in the strongest possible terms... acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans", the Élysée Palace said. Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said it was "unacceptable" and "shocking". "The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she said in a statement on Facebook. "Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety." Macron spoke to his Bulgarian counterpart on the sidelines of a European summit in Brussels, assuring her that "these acts would not go unpunished", the Élysée said. Several hundred Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski fans were gathered. Fighting broke out, with several Marseille fans wearing face coverings, an AFP journalist at the scene said. - 'Violent times' - "Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," the Marseille police prefecture told AFP. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds." The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests". Iotova said: "The French authorities must clarify the circumstances surrounding the attacks and look for responsibility from those who committed them, and UEFA should check how the safety of the Bulgarian fans at the stadium was ensured. "We are ready to provide the necessary assistance to our compatriots. This behaviour is unacceptable!" Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. "It's a very regrettable episode -- these are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski coach Julio Velazquez. "I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I'm very saddened by this situation." Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents". There were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break. "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable," said Marseille coach Bruno Génésio. The home team went on to win the game 1-0. stt/jc/nf/cms/pst

top.title: Eagles Security Forced to Step In as Nick Sirianni Appears to Confront Cowboys Fans After Historic Thanksgiving Win
top.description: Nick Sirianni ©IMAGO/Newscom World The Philadelphia Eagles seem to have finally caught a break this season. With a thrilling end to the Dallas Cowboys game on Thursday, head coach Nick Sirianni has plenty of reasons to celebrate. However, he might have gotten a bit too excited. As seen in the clips , doing rounds on social media, Sirianni is captured heading straight towards the Dallas fans with an agitated look after the win. Philadelphia’s chief security officer Domenico DiSandro, aka Big Dom, rushed to the scene to pull the head coach away from the crowd. Sirianni tried to charge back in. The heated rivalry between the two sides had the heat turned up with Sirianni celebrating the victory right in front of the home crowd. The Eagles head coach was so amped up after the win that he only gave a side hug to Dallas head coach Brian Schottenheimer, as part of the customary gesture after games. He didn’t even spare the losing coach a second glance and walked away right after. When a head coach's emotions boil over on the biggest stage, it reveals the intensity behind a dominant performance. Stay subscribed for the untold stories shaping the NFL's fiercest rivalries. What initially looked like a comfortable Cowboys victory turned into a stunning Eagles comeback, with Dallas surrendering a 31-10 lead before falling 39-38. Jake Elliott delivered the decisive blow with a 59-yard field goal with just two seconds remaining. The 21-point comeback was the largest ever in Thanksgiving game history for the NFL. The comeback was also made possible by an outstanding performance from Joe Milton, who delivered the best outing of his career. The Eagles quarterback threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns while adding a rushing score. In the fourth quarter alone, Philadelphia added 22 points. Dallas tried to stay in the fight with a crazy touchdown from Dak Prescott, who was briefly in the air but managed to hang on to the ball for the score. However, it was all in vain, as Brandon Aubrey missed a field goal later on. This is not the first time that Big Dom had to step up and calm Sirianni down. Back in 2024, the Eagles head coach got into a heated fight with Washington Commanders tight end Zach Ertz as they shook hands after the game. Even though the Eagles wrote one of the best comeback wins on Thanksgiving, the head coach’s reaction did not sit well with many. “Nick Sirianni is classless and should not be an NFL head coach,” Dr. Jeff Mueller wrote on X. “Buddy needs a nap and an ice cream sandwich to go chill out.” Walking back into the stadium after the game, that energy was still present in Sirianni. “We know how to fight,” he can be heard saying as he walks past the media. He also celebrated with Eagles fans nearby before he walked back in, high-fiving them. It all came about in a matter of minutes for Philadelphia, who were on a seven-game losing streak not long ago. Sirianni has reason to celebrate, but he sure will be asked about his behavior with the fans

top.title: Tom Brady rips into Aaron Rodgers for breaking ‘the sanctity of an NFL locker room’
top.description: Another Hall of Fame quarterback is coming out against Aaron Rodgers’ recent comments. This time it was Tom Brady, who kept it professional but made clear that Rodgers’ takedown of the Steelers after his benching needed to stay in house. “The sanctity of an NFL locker room, it’s a very sacred place,” Brady said on the Fox broadcast of the Eagles’ 39-38 win over the Cowboys on Thanksgiving in Dallas. “We shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together. Shouldn’t always be the place for private things to become public, that’s what I’ll say.” Fox Sports broadcast analyst Tom Brady looks on before the 49ers’ win over the Cowboys on Nov. 15, 2026, in Arlington, Texas. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Steelers announced on Tuesday night that they were benching Rodgers against the Broncos in favor of Mason Rudolph, and Rodgers responded on Wednesday by going scorched earth on head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show.” Among Rodgers’ gripes was the 19-year coach falling asleep in team meetings and leading a “1, 2, 3, Packers” chant after a huddle. The Steelers cut Rodgers soon after the appearance on “McAfee,” and he cleared waivers Thursday to become a free agent. Brady, who knows a thing or two about working with longtime coaches, acknowledged that feuds can happen in the locker room, but that doesn’t mean things need to boil over like they did in Pittsburgh. “I wasn’t a perfect player, [Bill Belichick] wasn’t a perfect coach, but we did some things in the game that we’re so proud of now,” Brady said. “And even me being four years removed from the game, things that matter more than winning a Super Bowl or trophy is my relationship with my teammates, my coaches. That’s going to transcend anything you do on the field. “It’s just unfortunate. I hate it, I hate to be even talking about it. It’s a privilege to be in the NFL. You want to inspire the next generation of athletes, and you always want to do it the right way.” Aaron Rodgers wears a frustrated expression during the Steelers’ loss to the Eagles on Nov. 22, 2026, in Philadelphia. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Brady wasn’t the only NFL legend who had something to say Thursday on Fox. Michael Strahan, Howie Long, and former Steelers quarterback Terry Bradshaw took time out of the pregame show to discuss Rodgers’ comments. While Rodgers now has the ability to sign with any team, his release by the Steelers may spell the end of his NFL career. ESPN insider Adam Schefter reported Thursday that it’s unlikely Rodgers finds a landing spot to finish out the season.

top.title: ‘This is unbelievable’: Stephen A. Smith shocked by what happened to the Cowboys against the Eagles
top.description: Photo by Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images for SiriusXM Stephen A. Smith always enjoys the Dallas Cowboys losing, but even he was shocked by their collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles. Thanksgiving games are always a joy to watch, and Cowboys fans would’ve felt really comfortable with the way their team played for large parts of the game. However, a late collapse saw them lose 39-38 to the Eagles, who pulled off the biggest comeback win on Thanksgiving in NFL history. Stephen A. Smith shocked by the Dallas Cowboys’ collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles The Dallas Cowboys looked to be in the driving seat to pick up a comfortable win against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday. The hosts dominated the first half and went in with a 28-10 lead at halftime. Midway through the fourth quarter, they were up 38-24 and could almost taste victory. However, the Eagles stayed alive via a blocked punt return TD, long touchdown bombs from Joe Milton to DeVonta Smith, and a game-winning push in the final minutes. Philadelphia pulled off a remarkable comeback to win 39-38 in the end, and Smith expressed his shock in the final moments of the game. He tweeted: “You can’t make this up! I can’t believe that the Dallas Cowboys are even in a position to lose this game. This is unbelievable!” Smith then posted a video of himself on X , laughing throughout and mocking the Cowboys after their disastrous collapse on Thursday night. The defeat is a massive blow for the Cowboys, who came into the game with a 5-6 record, and it just got worse. Their playoff hopes have been severely dented now. To add insult to injury, it was former Cowboy Milton who helped inflict the defeat, which must hurt even more. Up next for Dallas is a tough game against the Seattle Seahawks on the road. It remains to be seen how they will bounce back from such an embarrassing defeat. top.title: Jerry Jones hesitant to make major changes despite 'numbing' loss to Eagles
top.description: Jerry Jones hesitant to make major changes despite 'numbing' loss to Eagles originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jerry Jones is more accessible than most NFL owners, to the point that he reliably speaks with the media after each game. For Cowboys fans, that's a blessing and a curse; they get to hear an immediate response from the owner, but the words aren't always what they want to hear. After Dallas inexplicably blew a 21-point lead to the division-rival Eagles on Thursday, Jones was blunt about the shocking defeat but didn't offer much in the way of potential changes. Here's a look at what Jones had to say. MORE: Joe Milton likely secured NFL future with win over Cowboys Jerry Jones responds to Cowboys' collapse Jones called the loss to the Eagles "numbing" but said he "wouldn't anticipate" coaching changes despite the long layoff before the Cowboys' next game. "We can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games and be competitive, in my mind, without coaching changes at this time," Jones said. That came with a caveat, though. Jones said "nothing we've seen out here tonight" gives him confidence in coach Brian Schottenheimer, but he added, "You've got to look at everything," noting that there are "several more games to go." Cowboys owner Jerry Jones says that “nothing we saw out there tonight” gives him confidence in Brian Schottenheimer, but he reiterates that a change is not on his mind right now. https://t.co/BipwLyTsE9 — Nick Harris (@NickHarrisFWST) November 27, 2026 As for the game itself, Jones was clear that everyone on the team, from himself to the players, shared responsibility. "It was ours to take, and we didn't," Jones said. "You have to question everything." QB Dak Prescott agreed with Jones' assessment of the loss. Told that Jones called the defeat "numbing," Prescott told reporters, "That's a good description for how I'm feeling right now." The Cowboys have yet to win back-to-back games this season, and they now trail the Giants by four games in the loss column. Jones typically resists coaching changes as long as possible, but the questions surrounding Schottenheimer aren't likely to fade anytime soon after a Thanksgiving collapse. top.description: Jamal Musiala signals to the bench with injury. (Alexandra BEIER) Bayern Munich head to Hamburg on Saturday in the middle of a crisis which threatens not only to derail the club's sporting ambitions, but their identity itself. Bayern, who are in the midst of an injury crisis which has decimated their forward line including Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane, sit two points behind Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga table. But Bayern's treatment of midfielder Jamal Musiala by their hierarchy has led to a growing rift between the club and the playing group. Shortly after Bayern lost 2-1 to Lille on Wednesday, ending their run as the final unbeaten team in Europe's top-five leagues this season, vice-captain Joshua Kimmich suggested the club had fallen out of step with their values. "It's completely unacceptable and is not Bayern-like," Kimmich said on Wednesday, adding that Musiala's treatment was inconsistent with the club's "sense of togetherness". - 'Mia san mia' - This week, Bayern's hierarchy suggested Musiala take a pay cut as the 23-year-old battles his way back from a neurological condition which causes absence seizures. While the condemnation from media, player unions and former players was swift, Kimmich -- who was wearing the captain's armband with Manuel Neuer out injured -- was the first member of Bayern's current squad to speak out. Despite their status as one of football's perennial heavyweights, Bayern have always sought to emphasise their Bavarian roots and member-ownership in contrast to the American and Gulf-owned behemoths that loom over the European landscape. But their cold-hearted treatment of Musiala, a fan-favourite and popular inside the dressing room, threatens their carefully crafted identity. top.title: Verstappen spells out what truly puts him off racing in the Indy 500
top.description: Max Verstappen has revealed why he is unwilling to take part in the Indianapolis 500, citing the risks associated with oval racing and the serious accident suffered by Nelson Piquet at Indianapolis. The four-time Formula 1 world champion has made no secret of his ambitions to compete in other motorsport disciplines alongside his commitments with Red Bull Racing, with endurance racing among the Dutchman's main interests. However, despite his admiration for the Indianapolis 500, Verstappen is not particularly interested in testing himself at the prestigious American event. The Red Bull driver explained that his reluctance has nothing to do with doubts over his ability to be competitive, but rather with the risks involved. Verstappen cites Piquet's Indianapolis crash Speaking to the media ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Verstappen pointed to the accident suffered by three-time F1 world champion Piquet, the father of his partner Kelly, as one of the reasons behind his stance. The Brazilian suffered serious injuries to both legs and feet during practice for the 1992 Indianapolis 500, requiring extensive surgery and months of rehabilitation. Despite the severity of his injuries, Piquet returned to Indianapolis the following year and qualified for the race. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Verstappen stressed that witnessing the long-term consequences of Piquet's accident has influenced his attitude towards competing in the American showpiece. "It's not that I think I won't be good at it. It's just the risk management. That's why I don't want to do it," Verstappen explained. "I like watching it, but I also know there is a very high risk involved by crashing, and I have had plenty of examples. "Even, of course, my father-in-law had a big crash there. And seeing how he had to live for the rest of his life after that crash is some risk that I'm not willing to take while already doing F1 and racing in GT3." The Dutchman also explained that, given the risks he already exposes himself to through his commitments in both Formula 1 and GT3 racing, he sees little reason to add another potentially dangerous undertaking to his schedule. "At one point, you're taking already a lot of risk. So sometimes then it's good to also have a few weekends where you don't need to be on the limit all the time."

nigeria.title: Sexual violence: UK, Mirabel Centre push for stronger protection, Justice for survivors
nigeria.description: *Mrs Sanwo-Olu hails centre’s 10,000-Survivor Care Milestone By Henry Ojelu THE United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have called for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. The British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Mr Jonny Baxter, and founder of the Mirabel Centre, Itoro Eze-Anaba, made the call on Thursday at a reception and panel discussion in Lagos to mark the centre’s milestone of supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence. The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said the achievement deserved celebration but stressed that sexual violence remained a serious issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. He said: “We want to celebrate 10,000 survivors, but we also want to ensure that many more people are able to access the professional support and services they need.” Baxter emphasised the importance of placing survivors’ experiences at the centre of interventions, saying their voices were essential to understanding their challenges and improving access to support and justice. He reaffirmed the UK’s commitment to ending violence against women and girls through development partnerships and collaboration with governments and civil society organisations. He also disclosed that the UK would soon host an international summit on technology-facilitated gender-based violence, noting that emerging forms of abuse required new approaches and solutions. Earlier, Eze-Anaba acknowledged the contributions of the British Council, the Department for International Development and the British High Commission to the establishment and growth of the centre. She said the British High Commission funded the centre’s first three years and continued to support its work through partnerships and advocacy opportunities. Describing the milestone as more than a numerical achievement, she said the centre remained committed to delivering services with dignity and respect. “Today is not about public relations for the Mirabel Centre. It is about the services we provide and how those services are shared in a dignified manner for survivors,” she said. The survey also revealed that only 28 per cent of those affected reported their experiences, highlighting the extent of underreporting and the fear, stigma and discrimination that prevent victims from seeking help. nigeria.title: Fountain of Life Church challenges bench warrant against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya
nigeria.description: The Fountain of Life Church has raised concerns over the issuance of a bench warrant against its Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, by the Lagos State High Court, questioning the procedure leading to the order. In a statement dated November 26, 2026, the church said the development followed proceedings before Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin, which also culminated in the judge’s recusal from the case. The church claimed that Odukoya had not been formally served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or through substituted service, as directed by the court. It also alleged that directives contained in the court’s orders of November 18 and 23 concerning the service of the documents remained unfulfilled. According to the church, its legal representatives had already filed a Notice of Appeal and two separate motions challenging the orders, their enforcement, the court’s jurisdiction and the contempt proceedings. The church further claimed that the matter was not listed on the court’s cause list for November 26 and that members of the media were asked to leave the courtroom before the bench warrant was issued. It said the warrant was issued without the court first determining the pending applications, after which the presiding judge recused herself. “These developments occurred within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before 1 December 2026, the date originally fixed by the court for mention,” the statement said. The church described the circumstances as raising serious questions about due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice. It added that its lawyers were challenging the orders and related procedural and jurisdictional issues before the appropriate courts, including the Court of Appeal. Clarifying the implications of the warrant, the church said its issuance did not amount to a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute. The church also maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, describing the position as part of the issues being pursued through the judicial process. It urged members and the general public to remain calm, united and prayerful, adding that it would exhaust all available legal remedies within the Nigerian judicial system. business.title: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally The 2019 Lightning conference in Berlin was lit: five hundred “cypherpunks” getting each other high on visions of a future with peer-to-peer electronic cash. Attending a bitcoin conference back in the day felt like being a teenager at a friend’s party while their parents were out of town. It was exciting and new. The feeling was the opposite of FOMO: something big was happening, we were on the inside, and the rest of the world was going to envy us. It was the kind of party that you could only have when the adults weren’t looking. Whenever someone bought a beer (with bitcoin), everyone would hoot and holler and record it on their phones for Instagram/Twitter (it was still called Twitter). Lightning was the bleeding edge. We called it “the Lightning Network” (capitalized, if you please), and talking about it felt like talking about string theory: something so far out you’re not even sure it’s real. I spent a lot of time invoking the abacus . Those are the times some of us remember fondly and keep trying to relive at bitcoin conferences today. That’s why we engage in rituals like drone shows, Satoshi Rockamoto sets, beefsteak dinners , and video game tournaments for sats, but it’s not the same. The ratio of bitcoin OG speakers to suits is shifting. Many event rooms are half empty, and the halls and meeting rooms are full of people negotiating cap tables and profit-sharing splits. The adults haven’t shut the party down, but they have crashed it, and it kinda feels like their party now. The most exciting thing I noticed at the last bitcoin conference I attended was that nothing exciting happened. And that’s worth celebrating. From Tech Subcultures to Mainstream Tech Adoption The road to boring is seldom smooth. Technological innovation benefits from passion and bold ideas. People work harder on a project when they feel strongly about it and identify closely with like-minded collaborators. That’s where tech subcultures, their rituals, and their dogmas come from. But such passion and tribalism feed conflict, at least for a while until the tech goes mainstream, and normies, who couldn’t care less about subculture squabbles, take over. This progression from an exciting new technology that inspires strong emotions to a humdrum utility is not unusual. World-changing innovations often (always?) start with a committed subculture that identifies fiercely with their weird tech before the mainstream adopts it and soon expects it. In fact, this trajectory has become the standard doctrine of tech marketing. For example, in the early days of the internet, early adopters wrote a Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace , picking a fight with states and corporations despite having nothing to back it up but chatrooms and dreams. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Born in Zaria and originally from Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967, eventually rising to become Deputy Managing Director of the Anambra Broadcasting Service. He went on to feature in hundreds of films, including Igodo , The Egg of Life and Lionheart . Survived by his wife, Josephine, and their six children, including actors Linc and Yul Edochie , he leaves behind a remarkable body of work. As we remember his life and contribution to Nigerian cinema, here are five films that capture some of the performances that made Pete Edochie a household name. Things Fall Apart (1987) Before Nollywood’s home-video boom even began, Pete Edochie became a household name across Nigeria and internationally through his breakout role as Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s classic novel Things Fall Apart. Directed by David Orere , the acclaimed television miniseries marked Edochie’s first professional acting role and saw him bring the proud, fierce, and deeply conflicted Umuofia warrior to life with remarkable nuance. His performance was so transformative that, for generations of viewers, Edochie and Okonkwo became inseparable. entertainment.description: After more than 30 years of experience in the fashion industry, the entrepreneur is bringing her experience to a Nigerian clothing brand built on a simple proposition: quality should not have to come at an exorbitant price. In fashion, the conversation often begins with style, but it rarely ends there. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. For Alero Ebigbeyi, these are not just considerations; they are the principles shaping her latest venture, HÉYCH. The Nigerian fashion and clothing brand officially opened its retail store on November 10, bringing together fashion enthusiasts, media executives, influencers, friends and industry personalities for an introduction to the brand and its collections. Guests explored the space, examined the clothing and made purchases. Yet, amid the excitement of the launch, two observations kept coming up: the quality of the pieces and their affordability. It was a response that reflected the thinking behind HÉYCH, a brand seeking to occupy an important space in the market by making well-made, stylish clothing accessible without asking consumers to compromise on quality. For Ebigbeyi, this approach is informed by more than three decades of experience in the fashion industry. With over 30 years of experience in this industry, I understand the importance of quality, production standards and delivering value to customers,” she says. Rethinking How Fashion Is Produced That understanding is reflected in one of the brand’s most significant decisions: its investment in local manufacturing. Behind HÉYCH’s retail offering is a manufacturing facility in Lagos, a strategic investment that gives the brand greater control over production while creating the capacity to fulfil orders in large quantities. For Ebigbeyi, local production is as much about business efficiency as it is about building something sustainable within Nigeria. entertainment.title: Nollywood Legend Pete Edochie Passes Away at 79
entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). entertainment.description: Williams Alamu marks his B.Sc. First-Class Honours graduation in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. sports.title: Five Levski fans taken to hospital as presidents condemn Marseille violence
sports.description: Marseille police said 11 people were injured in the clashes, all of them Bulgarian (Justine MEDDAH) Five Levski Sofia supporters were taken to hospital after violence ahead of the Europa League game at Marseille on Thursday, with the French and Bulgarian presidents blaming the home fans. The lead-up to the match at the Stade Vélodrome was marred by confrontations in the stands between the two sets of fans, including the throwing of projectiles and flares. French President Emmanuel Macron condemned "in the strongest possible terms... acts of violence targeting Bulgarian fans", the Élysée Palace said. Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said it was "unacceptable" and "shocking". "The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she said in a statement on Facebook. "Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety." Macron spoke to his Bulgarian counterpart on the sidelines of a European summit in Brussels, assuring her that "these acts would not go unpunished", the Élysée said. Several hundred Marseille fans ran from the stand where they were situated about 10 minutes before kick-off, appearing to pursue a group of Bulgarian supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, where around 500 Levski fans were gathered. Fighting broke out, with several Marseille fans wearing face coverings, an AFP journalist at the scene said. - 'Violent times' - "Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," the Marseille police prefecture told AFP. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds." The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests". Iotova said: "The French authorities must clarify the circumstances surrounding the attacks and look for responsibility from those who committed them, and UEFA should check how the safety of the Bulgarian fans at the stadium was ensured. "We are ready to provide the necessary assistance to our compatriots. This behaviour is unacceptable!" Security personnel eventually managed to restore calm as the game kicked off on time. "It's a very regrettable episode -- these are incidents which are unacceptable for football," said Levski coach Julio Velazquez. "I support the fans who were caught up in this incident. I hope nothing serious has happened. I'm very saddened by this situation." Ligue 1 club Marseille said it was "working to understand the precise circumstances of these incidents". There were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break. "We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable," said Marseille coach Bruno Génésio. The home team went on to win the game 1-0. stt/jc/nf/cms/pst

It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together. Brady, who knows a thing or two about working with longtime coaches, acknowledged that feuds can happen in the locker room, but that doesn’t mean things need to boil over like they did in Pittsburgh. “I wasn’t a perfect player, [Bill Belichick] wasn’t a perfect coach, but we did some things in the game that we’re so proud of now,” Brady said. “And even me being four years removed from the game, things that matter more than winning a Super Bowl or trophy is my relationship with my teammates, my coaches. sports.title: Verstappen spells out what truly puts him off racing in the Indy 500
sports.description: Max Verstappen has revealed why he is unwilling to take part in the Indianapolis 500, citing the risks associated with oval racing and the serious accident suffered by Nelson Piquet at Indianapolis. The four-time Formula 1 world champion has made no secret of his ambitions to compete in other motorsport disciplines alongside his commitments with Red Bull Racing, with endurance racing among the Dutchman's main interests. However, despite his admiration for the Indianapolis 500, Verstappen is not particularly interested in testing himself at the prestigious American event. The Red Bull driver explained that his reluctance has nothing to do with doubts over his ability to be competitive, but rather with the risks involved. Verstappen cites Piquet's Indianapolis crash Speaking to the media ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Verstappen pointed to the accident suffered by three-time F1 world champion Piquet, the father of his partner Kelly, as one of the reasons behind his stance. The Brazilian suffered serious injuries to both legs and feet during practice for the 1992 Indianapolis 500, requiring extensive surgery and months of rehabilitation. Despite the severity of his injuries, Piquet returned to Indianapolis the following year and qualified for the race. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Verstappen stressed that witnessing the long-term consequences of Piquet's accident has influenced his attitude towards competing in the American showpiece. "It's not that I think I won't be good at it. It's just the risk management. That's why I don't want to do it," Verstappen explained. "I like watching it, but I also know there is a very high risk involved by crashing, and I have had plenty of examples. "Even, of course, my father-in-law had a big crash there. And seeing how he had to live for the rest of his life after that crash is some risk that I'm not willing to take while already doing F1 and racing in GT3." The Dutchman also explained that, given the risks he already exposes himself to through his commitments in both Formula 1 and GT3 racing, he sees little reason to add another potentially dangerous undertaking to his schedule. "At one point, you're taking already a lot of risk. So sometimes then it's good to also have a few weekends where you don't need to be on the limit all the time."

technology.title: The token factory never sleeps
technology.description: Agentic AI has supercharged demand for inference infrastructure. According to Goldman Sachs, token consumption is set to jump 24-fold to 120 quadrillion tokens per month between this year and 2030. Enterprises, wary of frontier model sticker shock, are now building their own GPU estates to cope. Those enterprises shouldn't blindly follow hyperscalers' lead when taking AI inference kit into production. The indicators of success for such companies are different than those for a frontier model provider, and so are the constraints. DIY AI infrastructure at the enterprise level has to earn ROI quickly, meaning that enterprises must focus on sustained operation. That makes engineering criteria such as uptime, heat and power, service windows, and deployment times doubly important. The performance benchmarks that hyperscalers focus on won't matter nearly as much to the average bank or retailer. ASUS is presenting the ASUS NVIDIA HGX Rubin System , built on the NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 platform, as a worked example of sustained AI inference infrastructure. It announced two models at NVIDIA GTC Berlin in October: the 3U hybrid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BHFS and the 2U fully liquid-cooled XR R1I12B-M1BLFS . Agents change the compute bill Agents represent a hockey stick curve for token consumption because an agent isn't a single prompt. It loops until the job's done, often spawning other versions of itself in the process. This is how it breaks a goal into steps and works through them iteratively. While training is a batch workload, agent inference is a production service that runs around the clock and only gets bigger. NVIDIA is making each generation of systems more powerful than the last to keep up with the demands of both. Running at scale, day after day, is another matter. A useful way to think about the infrastructure that does it is as a token factory: it takes in power, data and GPU compute and turns out tokens. What counts is throughput, meaning how many tokens, and how many users, the same power and floor space can serve, hour after hour. Enterprises move from pilots to AI factories Enterprises are moving ahead quickly with their AI factory projects. According to Deloitte's AI infrastructure survey , published in March, 64 percent of respondents have started limited or at-scale AI factory deployments, while 88 percent expect to do so by 2028. They are spending more on AI infrastructure to do it: 86 percent expect their budgets to increase over the next three years. Enterprises have different problems from hyperscalers and frontier model companies, though. Model builders often get to design greenfield campuses around their GPUs. technology.title: Microsoft: Hackers in China, N Korea using ARTEX AI tool to break into global tech systems
technology.description: Chinese and North Korean state-sponsored hacking crews are among the growing number of groups known for using the ARTEX pentesting tool in attacks, Microsoft said this week. ARTEX is an open source, AI-powered penetration testing framework that attackers have adopted to automate reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation since its public release in July. Campaigns that have been linked to ARTEX have targeted cloud environments, IT software like ConnectWise , and financial institutions globally, sometimes reaching privileged access in under three hours. Salt Typhoon is arguably the most recognizable name on the list of ARTEX beneficiaries – the group responsible for attacks on telcos AT&T and Verizon , US government systems , UK prime minister's aides , and more. The lesser-known Crystal Typhoon – the group behind the ArcaneDoor attacks back when Microsoft called it Storm-1849 – was also named alongside it, as were North Korea's Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet. Microsoft also named China-state-aligned Storm-0940, linked to the ConnectWise compromise, and financially motivated, Cambodia-based Storm-3358. It had previously reported both groups' use of ARTEX. Chinese cybersecurity company ThreatBook claimed ownership of ARTEX in November. GitHub user "Autumn-27" originally published its source code with a Chinese-language interface in July. Various forks of the repo, which was taken down in October, have meant that the same framework is available in multiple languages. According to Infrawatch , there are more than 130 variants of ARTEX in circulation, and it is the most widely used agentic offensive framework (AOF) at present. Like other offensive security tools adopted by criminals, ARTEX can lower the effort required to mount attacks. Experienced groups can also use it to automate repetitive work and pursue multiple avenues at once. As Microsoft echoed this week, after the FBI and AWS issued their warnings earlier this month , ARTEX is proving to be a useful tool for the more sophisticated groups to streamline and hasten their attacks too. It's being used to help attackers steal AI and cloud credentials at "industrial scale," as AWS put it, which provide attackers access to advanced models for free. Microsoft says ARTEX can progress from reconnaissance to persistent, privileged access within minutes, depending on its configuration and the target's defenses. technology.title: Tech's outage problem needs maintenance, not conspiracy theories
technology.description: Years of technical debt, increasingly complex systems, and underinvestment in IT operations have left organizations vulnerable to major outages, according to Forrester. The analyst pointed to a seven-day stretch in November when failures disrupted Microsoft 365, US air traffic control, banking, and other critical services. The coinciding outages provoked "a slew of conspiracy theories about cyberattacks and AI," Forrester said. "The real culprit is tragically mundane: the culmination of decades of technical debt, the frenetic buildout of massively complex and highly interdependent systems, the concentration of risk, and the underinvestment in advanced operations." Forrester urged technology suppliers and in-house IT teams to prioritize resilience as their systems grow more complex. Otherwise, "the tech estate will collapse like a house of cards, taking down consumer and business trust with it." Earlier this month, Microsoft was left struggling to restore many of its cloud services after a core process running on some servers became "overwhelmed" and its attempts to fix the problem failed. Some of its services did not recover for another 24 hours. In October, Google Cloud blamed a "power event" for taking down multiple online products for customers in Western Europe. Affected services included BigQuery Data Transfer Service, Cloud Filestore, Cloud Run, Google App Engine, and Google Kubernetes Engine. In October last year , a major outage impacted Amazon Web Services (AWS), with even Amazon's own web page reported to be offline and dozens of other online services and websites affected. Aviation and banking were also hit this month. A communications outage triggered a nationwide ground stop in the US on November 13 , while incidents involving JPMorgan Chase, United Airlines, Apple, Workday, Gmail, and other services added to the sense of widespread instability. "Claims that these were all part of one connected cyberattack or conspiracy are highly unlikely. The real story is much more mundane," the report said . Forrester argued that organizations have prioritized visible improvements over repairs to the underlying technology. "Modernization investments have favored visible change over structural renewal," wrote report authors Lauren Nelson and Mark Moccia. "Organizations routinely fund new customer experiences, cloud migrations, platform consolidation, and AI initiatives because leaders can connect them to growth or productivity. "They are less enthusiastic about updating core systems, simplifying architectures, retiring obsolete components, and eliminating fragile interfaces. The result is a modern front end resting on an aging, brittle, and increasingly interconnected estate." Forrester's recommendations are to map dependencies, test failures and recovery under realistic conditions, and use incidents and near misses to identify weaknesses before they cause another outage. ®

technology.title: Rackspace pulls plug on Spot cloud service after security breach
technology.description: Rackspace is shutting down its low-cost Spot cloud service after a security breach, giving customers two weeks' notice to move their workloads and retrieve their data. In a notice posted on Tuesday , the cloud computing biz said its Rackspace Spot service will cease operations at 1700 Central Time (2300 UTC) on December 8. Any workloads still running at that point will be terminated, and customers will no longer be able to access their data. "Following the recent security incident affecting Rackspace Spot, Rackspace has made the decision to wind down the service," the company said. "Spot customers are being notified with the wind-down timeline, instructions for retrieving their data and steps to secure their environments." Customers will have to contend with the fallout from the breach while simultaneously trying to get their applications and data off the platform. According to a customer notification seen by The Register , the attackers used leaked credentials to access parts of Rackspace Spot over a period of almost 22 hours on November 17. Rackspace only learned of the intrusion the following day, after a customer raised the alarm. The intruders impersonated legitimate users, created pods in customer Kubernetes clusters, gained access to stored credentials known as Kubernetes Secrets, and listed nodes and storage volumes. "With that access, they could have read any Secret in an affected user's clusters, and any Spot API token or refresh token that user held," Rackspace told customers. Rackspace has since revoked the affected tokens and sessions, removed the pods planted by the intruders, and changed the affected platform and storage keys. Customers must also reissue API tokens, download new Kubernetes configuration files, and rotate credentials stored in their clusters, including database passwords and third-party API keys. Sirish Raghuram, co-founder and chief growth officer of Platform9, which co-developed Spot with Rackspace, shed some light on the root cause in a November 20 GitHub post. "An observability system was breached using a compromised credential," Raghuram wrote. "This was obviously a critical error on our part and we are very sorry we let this happen." Raghuram said the incident necessitated significant changes to the underlying infrastructure clusters, prolonging the outage. Spot's selling point was cheap compute. The service operated an auction-based pricing model, allowing customers to bid for cloud infrastructure at a fraction of the cost of conventional on-demand instances. Rackspace advertised savings of up to 90 percent for customers willing to tolerate interruptions to their workloads. A permanent interruption probably wasn't what they had in mind. Rackspace hasn't explained why it chose closure over recovery, revealed how many customers were affected, or said whether it will offer migration extensions. It did not respond to The Register's questions. ®

technology.title: Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack

Peninsula Energy said it believes the attack is "confined to the plant and wellfield operating and control systems," and that back-office functions, such as payroll and other corporate systems, in both the US and Australia, remain unaffected. "The company's immediate priorities have been to protect the safety of its employees, secure its operating systems, and work towards the restoration of operations in a safe and controlled manner," it said in an update to the Australian Securities Exchange. The notification [PDF] went on to say that Peninsula Energy's investigations into the attack, including whether any data was compromised, remain ongoing. Peninsula has not given a restart date and says it cannot yet assess the impact on its 2027 production guidance. Operations will remain suspended until recovery and safety checks are complete. "Peninsula will provide further updates to the market as material information becomes available," it said. The disclosure of additional information came two days after Peninsula secured a short trading halt, which referenced a cybersecurity incident at its Wyoming site. The November 23 filing [PDF] dated the incident to Friday evening in Western Australia. Wednesday's update clarified that Strata detected it on the morning of November 20, local US time. Peninsula subsequently requested a voluntary suspension of trading until the earlier of November 30 or an announcement on restarting operations and any resulting change to production guidance. Peninsula's Lance project is a uranium mining operation, extracting the element from underground deposits and turning it into uranium concentrate, aka yellowcake or U₃O₈. Uranium concentrate is feedstock for nuclear fuel production, typically undergoing conversion, enrichment, and fabrication into uranium dioxide pellets before use in reactors. The Lance central processing plant was constructed to produce a maximum of 2.0 million pounds (Mlb) of U₃O₈ annually, and is licensed for 3.0 Mlb. Peninsula previously forecast production of 500,000 to 600,000 pounds in 2027, having withdrawn its 2026 guidance earlier this year following operational problems at Lance. It now says it will reassess the 2027 outlook once operations resume. ®

technology.title: Company was religious about backups but sinned by leaving them exposed
technology.description: Welcome, once again, to PWNED, where we’re thankful every time someone leaves a password sticky note on a monitor or fails to delete a terminated employee’s admin account. But neither of those common occurrences is what we’ll be talking about today. Instead, our subject broke the number-one rule of backups: you gotta keep ’em separated. Our story comes courtesy of Da Li, who serves as global alliance manager at Info2Soft , a company that provides data protection and recovery software. At one point, a partner called him into a case where a Chinese vehicle parts manufacturer fell victim to a ransomware gang. Unfortunately, its backup was compromised too. The manufacturer had religiously backed up its manufacturing execution system (MES) and SAP orders, inventory, and finance systems every night. There was even a green dashboard that showed the backup process had succeeded, and someone checked that every morning. However, one Friday evening, crims broke into the network and found out that the backup server was joined to the same Windows domain as the rest of the network. The hackers found a plaintext password for the backup service account in a maintenance script on a file share and discovered that someone had used the very same password for a domain admin account. So the first thing the crooks did was delete every restore point on that backup server. Then they started encrypting the production servers to ransom them. “Every backup job had succeeded for three years,” Li said. “The failure was that the thing meant to save them could be reached with the same keys as the thing being attacked.” The results were devastating. With the MES and SAP data both gone, the plant couldn't schedule production, ship parts, or track them. By the time Li was called in, the plant had already resolved its ransomware situation. We don’t know whether it paid or not. The manufacturer did ask Li and his company to make sure that this couldn’t happen again. Li’s fix was not radical, but it was instructive. He made sure that the company now keeps its backup system outside the production domain, uses unique credentials, and requires MFA to reduce the risk of unauthorized access even if a password is compromised. He also made sure that the company keeps at least one offline backup and runs a test restore quarterly to ensure it’s prepared for emergencies.®

science.title: Venus shines at its brightest in the predawn sky this week. Here's where to look
science.description: null Venus is at its most dazzling in the predawn sky this week as it shines close to the bright star Spica in the southeast. Here's what you need to know. As an inner planet, Venus never strays far from the horizon, at least compared to outer planets like Jupiter and Mars which can be visible all night long during opposition, when they shine opposite the sun in Earth's sky. Instead, Venus alternates between morning and evening appearances. All the while, its shifting moon-like phases and ever-changing proximity to Earth causes its brightness to wax and wane. When is Venus at its most dazzling? Venus will reach peak brightness during its current morning apparition at 1:37 p.m. EST (1837 GMT) on Nov. 27 according to the astronomy website In-The-Sky . Stargazers in the U.S. could get an incredible view of Venus in the predawn hours of the coming week, as the planet climbs into the southeastern sky ahead of the rising sun, with Mercury clinging close to the horizon below. Celestron Nexstar 4SE (Image credit: Celestron) This is a fantastic go-to telescope with a 4-inch aperture and can help you quickly find a steady view of the moon. For a closer look at craters and the terminator, make sure to grab a 9mm or 12mm eyepiece and get stronger magnification. _ Celestron Nexstar 4SE review The bright star Spica will glow less than five degrees away from Venus before dawn on Nov. 27 — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length against the night sky. Spica is a double system of two stars that orbit one another once every four days. Its stars are separated by just approximately 11 million miles (less than 18 million kilometers), making them far too close to split visually with even the most powerful amateur equipment. However, the system still makes for a dazzling target, appearing as a magnificent blue-white star when viewed through the eyepiece of a 4-inch telescope. Venus will appear close to Spica in the southeastern sky. (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) Check that the sun is safely below the horizon before turning your telescope on Venus to observe a crescent of light playing across the planet's dense atmosphere. Over the coming weeks and months, Venus will appear increasingly illuminated as it moves farther away from Earth in its orbit, while its apparent size through a telescope will gradually decrease. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 26, 2011: NASA's 2-ton nuclear-powered Curiosity rover launches to Mars
science.description: null On November 26, 2011, the NASA Curiosity rover launched to Mars. The Mars rover Curiosity was the biggest and most powerful rover anyone had ever sent to the Red Planet. The 2-ton science laboratory is about the size of a small SUV. The mission's goal was to search for habitable environments on Mars , or evidence that the planet could have been habitable in the past. It launched on an Atlas V rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. About nine months later, Curiosity made a challenging landing on Mars. It successfully used a new landing technology called a sky crane to gently lower it to the surface. NASA's Curiosity rover lifts off atop a United Launch Alliance Atlas V rocket on Nov. 26, 2011 from Florida's Cape Canaveral Air Force Station. (Image credit: collectSPACE/Robert Z. Pearlman ) Why it mattered It may be hard to imagine now, but 15 years ago, the idea of a nuclear-powered rover on Mars was just a concept. When the Curiosity rover launched in 2011, it made that idea a reality the car-size probe (using a plutonium-based radioisotope thermoelectric generator that converts heat from radioactive decay into power) as it headed to the Red Planet. Curiosity was the largest rover ever launched to Mars, following up on the success of the tiny Sojourner rover in 1997 and the larger twin rovers Spirit and Opportunity in 2004. Its sky crane landing system was novel at the time, and fully automated. Once it began its descent in August 2012, NASA could only wait through "seven minutes of terror" to see how it turned out. It ended being a huge success. NASA's Curiosity rover on Mars. (Image credit: NASA) After its smooth landing, Curiosity lived up to its original name: the Mars Science Laboratory. Within weeks, Curiosity fulfilled its primary mission. It found evidence of ancient running water on Mars . It later found organic molecules on Mars as well. Curiosity's primary mission was expected to last just about one Martian year (687 Earth days, or about two Earth years), as the rover explored its Gale Crater landing site. But NASA has extended the mission as the rover continues to operate in good health. In fact, Curiosity has survived long enough to welcome its successor to Mars, the Perseverance rover , which landed in February 2021 on a mission to collect the first samples for later retrieval. Perseverance used the same basic 2-ton design, plutonium power system and sky crane landing system to reach Mars. And today, a ground-based twin of the Curiosity rover, called Promise , is being outfitted for an upcoming mission to the moon. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.description: null Rocket Lab will add another satellite to a growing Japanese Earth-observation constellation today (Nov. 26), and you can watch the action live. An Electron rocket carrying a radar imaging satellite for Tokyo-based Earth-observation company Synspective is scheduled to lift off from Rocket Lab 's New Zealand launch site today, during a window that opens at 7:00 p.m. ET (0000 GMT and 1:00 p.m. on Nov. 27 in New Zealand). You can watch the mission, called "Night Owls Never Sleep," via Rocket Lab starting about 30 minutes before liftoff. Space.com will carry the company's stream if, as expected, it's made available. Synspective is building a network of "Strix" spacecraft equipped with synthetic aperture radar (SAR), which uses radio waves to generate detailed images of Earth's surface in both day and night lighting, as well as through cloud cover. Today's launch will be Rocket Lab's 14th for Synspective to date, and there are a lot more coming. At the end of September, Rocket Lab announced a deal with the company for an additional 20 Electron missions between 2028 and 2031 — the largest commercial launch contract in the rocket's history. That agreement brought Synspective's total number of contracted Electron flights to 47. Synspective aims to eventually establish a constellation capable of imaging locations anywhere on Earth at intervals of just a few hours. The patch for Rocket Lab's "Night Owls Never Sleep" mission. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) If all goes to plan today, the Electron's kick stage will deploy the Strix satellite into low Earth orbit , 569 kilometers (353.6 miles) above our planet. "Night Owl Never Sleeps" will be the 101st mission to date for Rocket Lab. Ninety-two of them have been orbital flights with Electron; the other nine have been missions with HASTE , a suborbital variant of Electron that allows customers to test sensors and other equipment in the hypersonic flight environment.

science.title: Cosmic 'betta fish' glows in spectacular nebula portrait | Space photo of the day for Nov. 26, 2026
science.description: null An image captured by the Dark Energy Camera showcasing the Betta Fish Nebula. (Image credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA) The striking blue of the Betta Fish Nebula swims across the cosmic landscape, a stunning wisp of material leftover from a stellar explosion. What is it? Roughly 6,800 light-years from Earth and nestled in the Centaurus constellation, this piece of the supernova remnant SNR G295.5+09.7 has earned the nickname the Betta Fish Nebula for its floaty, fishy shape. This almost ghostly whirl of gas and dust was created when a star much more massive than our sun exploded, blasting its outer layers of material outward in the process. Over time, the remnants of this supernova eruption stretched outward into space, dispersing and colliding with surrounding gas. The explosive remnants mixing with gas in the interstellar medium created this glowing, blue cloud. This celestial scene was captured by the Dark Energy Camera (DECam), that was created by the U.S. Department of Energy. The camera is installed on the National Science Foundation's Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope in Chile. Why is it incredible? This image of a colossal, cosmic "fish" was captured by a camera meant to study the illusive effects of dark energy , which is the name scientists have given for whatever mysterious something is causing the universe to expand at an accelerating rate . The camera is used as part of the Dark Energy Survey, a six-year, international collaboration in which scientists have collected observations of hundreds of millions of galaxies, thousands of supernova and additional details about our cosmos that could help to fill in the picture of the nature of dark energy. And while researchers this past January revealed the initial result of this six-year survey, scientists continue to explore the possibilities of dark energy with DECam alongside instruments like the recently-launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. However, while the survey has lofty goals with its DECam data, the camera can also capture beautiful imagery like this cerulean wisp thousands of light-years away.

science.title: Thanksgiving night sky 2026 — What to look for after dinner tonight
science.description: null If your household is like most American families, then on Thursday you likely will all be sitting down with family and friends for a traditional Thanksgiving turkey dinner during the mid-to-late afternoon hours. Then as darkness falls, some will probably migrate into the living room to catch some football or other holiday fare on television. But if you have a large gathering of family and friends at your home — and if your skies are mainly clear — why not invite everyone outside to gaze at the evening sky? If you have binoculars, or better yet, a telescope, you just might end up turning this into a memorable family tradition of its own. First, the "Lord of the Rings" . . . If I may paraphrase the mysterious voice from the 1989 movie, "Field of Dreams": "If you set up your telescope, they will come." And you'll get a big kick out of your Turkey Day guests uttering all the "oohs" and "ahs" or exclamations of "Wow!" with just one peek through the eyepiece. As darkness falls, Saturn will glow at first magnitude, shining with a sedate, yellow-white light and appearing noticeably brighter than the star Fomalhaut, about 40 degrees (the equivalent of four fist-widths) to its lower right.
